rationale: C22 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template for the child. Both letters first affirm broad Executive cooperation with congressional information requests, then invoke separation of powers and the President’s historical authority to withhold information, identify candid internal advice and communications as essential to effective administration, and direct that the requested material not be disclosed. The child substantially reproduces C22’s distinctive language and argumentative sequence while adapting it from Defense Department testimony and documents to an ICA evaluation report. C01 and C25 share the general refusal-to-disclose framework, but neither matches the child’s language and machinery as closely.

shared_material.child_excerpt: under the historic doctrine of the separation of powers between the three great branches of our Government, the Executive has a recognized Constitutional duty and power with respect to the disclosure of information
shared_material.parent_excerpt: it is essential to the successful working of our system that the persons entrusted with power in any one of the three great branches of Government shall not encroach upon the authority confided to the others. The ultimate responsibility for the conduct of the Executive Branch rests with the President.
shared_material.explanation: Both frame the disclosure decision as an incident of constitutional separation of powers and presidential responsibility for the Executive Branch.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The President has throughout our history ... withheld information when he found that the disclosure of what was sought would be incompatible with the national interest.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: throughout our history the President has withheld information whenever he found that what was sought was confidential or its disclosure would be incompatible with the public interest or jeopardize the safety of the Nation.
shared_material.explanation: This is a close verbal reuse of a distinctive historical-authority formulation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: It is essential to effective administration that employees of the Executive Branch be in a position to be fully candid in advising with each other on official matters
shared_material.parent_excerpt: it is essential to efficient and effective administration that employees of the Executive Branch be in a position to be completely candid in advising with each other on official matters
shared_material.explanation: The child nearly reproduces C22’s core justification for protecting deliberative communications.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The disclosure of conversations, communications or documents embodying or concerning such opinions and advice can accordingly tend to impair or inhibit essential reporting and decision-making processes
shared_material.parent_excerpt: it is not in the public interest that any of their conversations or communications, or any documents or reproductions, concerning such advice be disclosed
shared_material.explanation: Both extend protection across conversations, communications, and documents concerning internal advice.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Since the disclosure of the report requested by you would not be compatible with the national interest, I have forbidden that it be furnished
shared_material.parent_excerpt: you will instruct employees of your Department that ... they are not to testify to any such conversations or communications or to produce any such documents or reproductions
shared_material.explanation: Each culminates in a presidential instruction forbidding compliance with a congressional demand for protected Executive Branch material.
